  "text": "On the first cold morning of the year, Nora took her winter coat to the alterations shop.

“The pocket again?” Mr. Vale asked.

She pushed her hand through the lining and showed him her fingers.

“You carry keys in there.”

“Where should I carry them?”

He turned the coat over without answering.

For twenty years he had repaired its cuffs, replaced its buttons, and once removed a train ticket from between the lining and the wool. Nora had missed that train. She still remembered the price.

This time a handwritten notice stood beside the till: CLOSING FRIDAY.

“What will you do?” she asked.

“My daughter has plans.”

“Do you?”

He measured a piece of lining against the torn pocket.

“Not before Saturday.”

When Nora returned, the shop’s shelves were bare. Pale rectangles marked the wall where cotton reels had hung.

Mr. Vale brought out her coat.

“I made the pocket deeper,” he said.

She reached inside. Her hand disappeared to the wrist.

“How much?”

He shook his head.

“That’s no way to run a business.”

“Apparently.”

Outside, she found something in the repaired pocket: a small brass thimble. She went back, but he had locked the door and was carrying a box toward a waiting car.

“You’ve left this,” she called.

He patted his waistcoat, then took it from her.

“Nearly packed everything,” he said.

Nora held the car door while he settled the box on the back seat. Inside were scissors, chalk, and a biscuit tin full of buttons.

His daughter made room in the boot for another box.

“There's still the kettle,” she told him.

“I'll get it,” Nora said."
